descripcion_es: Research, the digital world and artificial intelligence.
resumen: Vocabulary for talking about scientific research, innovation, the internet and artificial intelligence. Useful for the news and for debates on technology regulation and productivity.

explicacion.texto: Many words are international, but the collocations change: you “carry out / conduct research” (not “make research”), and “research” is uncountable: you don't say “a research” or “researches”, but “a study” or “research projects”.

filas: research (uncountable)
systematic study to discover new knowledge (es: investigación)
They carried out research on vaccines.
researcher / scientist
a person who does research / an expert in science (es: investigador / científico)
Researchers found a new gene.
to conduct an experiment
to do a scientific test (es: realizar un experimento)
The team conducted several experiments.
findings
the results of a study (es: resultados, hallazgos)
The findings were published in Nature.
breakthrough
a sudden, important discovery (es: avance decisivo)
It was a major breakthrough in cancer research.
evidence (uncountable)
facts or data that show something is true (es: pruebas, datos empíricos)
There is little evidence that it works.
peer review
evaluation of a work by other experts in the field (es: revisión por pares)
The paper is under peer review.
R&D (research and development)
work to create new products and knowledge (es: I+D)
Firms should spend more on R&D.
patent
the legal right to be the only one to make or sell an invention (es: patente)
They filed a patent for the device.
innovation / cutting-edge
a new idea or method / the most advanced (es: innovación / de vanguardia)
It uses cutting-edge technology.
to develop / to launch
to create and improve / to put on the market (es: desarrollar / lanzar)
The company launched a new app.
artificial intelligence (AI)
computer systems that perform tasks needing human intelligence (es: inteligencia artificial, IA)
AI is changing many jobs.
machine learning
computers learning from data without explicit programming (es: aprendizaje automático)
Machine learning needs large datasets.
algorithm
a set of rules a computer follows to solve a problem (es: algoritmo)
The algorithm decides what you see.
data (uncountable or plural)
facts and figures collected for analysis (es: datos)
The data shows a clear trend.
device
a piece of electronic equipment (es: dispositivo)
Turn off all electronic devices.
software / hardware
programs / physical equipment (es: programas / equipos)
We need to update the software.
to download / to upload
to copy from the internet to your device / from your device to the internet (es: descargar / subir)
Upload the file to the cloud.
cybersecurity / data breach
protection of computer systems / unauthorised access to data (es: ciberseguridad / filtración de datos)
The bank suffered a data breach.
privacy
the right to keep your personal life and data to yourself (es: privacidad, intimidad)
Users are worried about their privacy.
digital divide
the gap in access to technology between groups (es: brecha digital)
The digital divide affects older people.
automation
the use of machines to do work instead of people (es: automatización)
Automation may replace routine jobs.
user-friendly
easy to use (es: fácil de usar)
The new website is very user-friendly.

items: “Technique” is a technique (a method); “technology” is technology; “technician” is a technician (es: el técnico).
“Computer science” = the academic discipline (es: informática); “computing” = the field in general (es: informática).

ejemplos.frase: Scientists have made a breakthrough in battery technology.
ejemplos.traduccion: Los científicos han logrado un avance decisivo en la tecnología de baterías.

ejemplos.frase: There is growing evidence that social media affects teenagers' sleep.
ejemplos.traduccion: Hay cada vez más datos de que las redes sociales afectan al sueño de los adolescentes.

ejemplos.frase: Spain spends less on R&D than the EU average.
ejemplos.traduccion: España gasta menos en I+D que la media de la UE.

ejemplos.frase: The hospital uses AI to detect tumours earlier.
ejemplos.traduccion: El hospital usa IA para detectar tumores antes.

ejemplos.frase: Millions of customers were affected by the data breach.
ejemplos.traduccion: Millones de clientes se vieron afectados por la filtración de datos.

ejemplos.frase: My grandmother finds her new phone surprisingly user-friendly.
ejemplos.traduccion: A mi abuela su móvil nuevo le resulta sorprendentemente fácil de usar.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: They are making a research on climate.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: They are doing research on climate.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Research” is uncountable and is used with do, carry out or conduct.

errores_hispanohablantes.bien: There is a lot of evidence.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Evidence” is uncountable; for a single item: “a piece of evidence”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: He works in the technology of the company.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: He works in the company's IT department.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The computer department (es: departamento de informática) is the “IT (department)”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I have to actualize the software.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I have to update the software.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “actualizar” is “update”; “actualize” means to make something real.

ejercicios.frase: The university is ___ research into renewable energy.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card stresses that what changes is the collocations: you say “carry out” or “conduct research”, never “make research”. The clue is the noun “research”, which in English combines with “carry out”, “conduct” or “do”. That is why it is “is carrying out research into renewable energy”, in the continuous because the research is in progress. Note also that “research” goes with “into” or “on”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: You say “carry out / conduct research”, not “make”.
ejercicios.traduccion: La universidad está llevando a cabo investigaciones sobre energías renovables.

por_opcion.carrying out: Correct: “carry out research” is the standard collocation (to do a piece of research).
por_opcion.making: Incorrect: it is a calque of Spanish “hacer una investigación”; “make research” is not used.
por_opcion.putting: Incorrect: “put” does not combine with “research”; it appears in other expressions such as “put forward a theory”.
por_opcion.taking: Incorrect: “take” combines with “a test” or “measures”, but not with “research”.

glosario.significado: llevar a cabo una investigación, investigar

ejercicios.frase: She published three researches last year.
respuestas: She published three studies last year.
She published three papers last year.
She published three research papers last year.
She published three pieces of research last year.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that “research” is uncountable: it takes neither “a” nor a plural. The clue is “three researches”, which tries to count it. To count pieces of research you must use a countable noun: “studies”, “papers” (scientific articles), “research papers” or the phrase “pieces of research”. Any of them corrects the sentence.
ejercicios.traduccion: Publicó tres estudios el año pasado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She published three researches last year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: “research” is uncountable and has no plural.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She published three research last year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Removing the -s is not enough: “research” is still uncountable and cannot go with a number.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She published three investigations last year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: An “investigation” is mainly a police or judicial inquiry; scientific works are “studies” or “papers”.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (a decisive advance).
ejercicios.frase: The new vaccine is a major ___ in medicine.
ejercicios.explicacion: The word in the table is “breakthrough”, a decisive advance, a discovery that opens a new path. The clue is “a major ___ in medicine”: you need a countable noun that expresses an important leap, and “major breakthrough” is a very frequent collocation. It comes from “break through”, to get through a barrier. “Advance” also exists, but it is more general.
ejercicios.traduccion: La nueva vacuna es un gran avance en medicina.

errores_previstos.explicacion: An “advance” is any step forward; for a decisive discovery the word required is “breakthrough”.
The noun is written as one word: “breakthrough”.
“Progress” is uncountable and does not take “a major”.

ejercicios.frase: There isn't enough ___ to prove the theory.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table marks “evidence” as uncountable: it means proof or empirical data, and it never takes -s or “an”. The clue is “There isn't enough”, in the singular, which fits an uncountable noun. That is why it is “enough evidence”. If you need to count, say “a piece of evidence”. Don't confuse it with “evident”, which is an adjective.
ejercicios.traduccion: No hay pruebas suficientes para demostrar la teoría.

por_opcion.evidence: Correct: an uncountable noun meaning proof or data.
por_opcion.evidences: Incorrect: “evidence” has no plural; it is the typical mistake on the card (“many evidences”).
por_opcion.evidents: Incorrect: “evident” is an adjective (es: evidente), and English adjectives have no plural.

ejercicios.frase: Remember to actualize the app before Monday.
respuestas: Remember to update the app before Monday.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is a false friend from the card's typical mistakes: to “actualizar” a program is “update”, whereas “actualize” means to make something real (for example, your own potential) and is rare. The clue is “the app”: we are talking about installing the latest version. The correct sentence is “Remember to update the app before Monday”. The noun is the same: “an update”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Acuérdate de actualizar la aplicación antes del lunes.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Remember to actualize the app before Monday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: “actualize” does not mean updating a program.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Remember to actualise the app before Monday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Changing to the British spelling fixes nothing: the correct verb is “update”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Remember to upload the app before Monday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Upload” is to put a file on the internet; to bring something up to date is “update”.

ejercicios.frase: Companies that invest in ___ tend to be more productive.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “R&D (research and development)” as the equivalent of Spanish “I+D”. The clue is “invest in ___” and the topic of productivity: it is the standard term in economics. The abbreviation “R&D”, the form “R and D” and the full expression “research and development” are all accepted. The letters look reversed compared with the Spanish ones, but the abbreviation stands for “investigación y desarrollo” all the same.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las empresas que invierten en I+D tienden a ser más productivas.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the Spanish abbreviation; in English it is “R&D”.
The order is “R&D”: first research and then development.
“Investigation” is not scientific research; the fixed form is “research and development”.

ejercicios.frase: Please ___ your CV to our website.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table distinguishes “to download” (from the internet to your computer) and “to upload” (from your computer to the internet). The clue is “to our website”: the CV goes from the candidate to the company's website. That is why it is “upload your CV”. If it went the other way, it would be “download a form from our website”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Putting a file on the internet is “upload”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Por favor, suba su currículum a nuestra web.

por_opcion.upload: Correct: to send a file from your device to the internet.
por_opcion.download: Incorrect: “download” is to bring a file from the internet to your device; the direction is the opposite.
por_opcion.load up: Incorrect: “load up” is to fill something (a car, a lorry), not to upload files.

ejercicios.frase: Rural areas suffer from the digital ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “digital divide”: the difference in access to the internet and technology between groups or areas. The clue is “Rural areas” and “digital ___”: rural areas tend to have a worse connection. “Digital gap” is also accepted, less common but correct. “Divide” here is a noun: a division, a separation.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The digital gap is the “digital divide” (also “digital gap”).
ejercicios.traduccion: Las zonas rurales sufren la brecha digital.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A “breach” is a security gap (data breach), not an inequality of access.
The fixed collocation is “digital divide”; “digital division” is not used with this meaning.

ejercicios.frase: The study's ___ were published in a leading journal.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “findings” as the results or discoveries of a piece of research; it is almost always plural. The clue is “The study's ___ were published”, which needs a plural noun related to a study. It comes from the verb “find”. A “journal” is a scientific journal, not a newspaper.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The results of a study are its “findings”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los resultados del estudio se publicaron en una revista de referencia.

por_opcion.findings: Correct: the results or discoveries of a study.
por_opcion.foundings: Incorrect: a “founding” is the establishment of something (a city, a company); besides, it is not used in the plural like this.
por_opcion.finds: Incorrect: “a find” is a physical discovery (an object found, for example in archaeology) or a bargain; it is not the results of a study.

ejercicios.frase: Children spend hours a day on their electronic ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “device”: a mobile phone, a tablet, a games console… The clue is “electronic ___” and the plural possessive “their”: you need a countable noun in the plural. That is why it is “devices”, with -s. It is the general word for any electronic gadget.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los niños pasan horas al día con sus dispositivos electrónicos.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The children have several gadgets and the meaning is plural: “devices”.
This is a calque from Spanish; the English word is “devices”.
“Devise” is a verb (to invent a plan); the noun is spelt with c: “devices”.

ejercicios.frase: She learned a new painting ___ at the workshop.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card distinguishes “technique” (a specific method), “technology” and “technician” (a skilled worker). The clue is “a new painting ___”: you learn a method for painting. That is why it is “technique”, with the article “a” because it is countable. “Workshop” here is a practical course.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aprendió una nueva técnica de pintura en el taller.

por_opcion.technique: Correct: a specific method or procedure for doing something.
por_opcion.technology: Incorrect: “technology” is machines and systems, not a painting method.
por_opcion.technic: Incorrect: “technic” is a rare, old-fashioned form; the normal word is “technique”.

glosario.significado: taller (curso práctico o lugar de trabajo)

ejercicios.frase: The hackers caused a massive data ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “data breach”, a security breach in which third parties access protected data. The clue is “hackers”, who attack systems, and “data ___”. “Data leak” is also accepted and very similar, although “leak” is used above all when information escapes or is disclosed. Both are countable nouns.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A data leak: “data breach” or “data leak”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los piratas informáticos provocaron una filtración de datos masiva.

errores_previstos.explicacion: “Filtration” is passing a liquid through a filter; for data it is “breach” or “leak”.
“Divide” is used in “digital divide” (inequality of access), not for a cyberattack.

glosario.significado: filtración de datos, brecha de seguridad

respuestas: Automation could replace many routine jobs
ejercicios.explicacion: The key word is “automation”, which the table links to replacing routine jobs. The order is that of any English sentence: subject (“Automation”, with a capital letter at the start) + modal “could” + verb “replace” + object. In the object, adjectives go before the noun: “many routine jobs”, with “many” first and “routine” just before “jobs”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Subject + modal + verb + object with its modifiers in front.
ejercicios.traduccion: La automatización podría sustituir muchos empleos rutinarios.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Automation could replace many jobs routine
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the Spanish order (“empleos rutinarios”); in English the modifier “routine” goes before “jobs”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Automation could replace routine many jobs
errores_previstos.explicacion: “Many” goes before the other modifiers: “many routine jobs”.

ejercicios.frase: The paper was rejected after ___ review.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “peer review”: other experts in the same field evaluate a work before it is published. The clue is “The paper was rejected after ___ review”, the selection process of scientific journals. “Peer” means an equal (someone at your level). It is pronounced like “pier”, and the trap in the option “pair” is phonetic.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Evaluation by fellow experts is “peer review”.
ejercicios.traduccion: El artículo fue rechazado tras la revisión por pares.

por_opcion.peer: Correct: “peer review” is review by other specialists at the same level.
por_opcion.pair: Incorrect: a “pair” is two things; it is the literal translation of Spanish “pares”, but it does not form the expression.
por_opcion.partner: Incorrect: a “partner” is an associate or a spouse; it forms no expression with “review” in this sense.

ejercicios.frase: The inventor filed a ___ for his new engine.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives “patent”, with the example “They filed a patent”. The clue is the verb “filed”, which in this context means to submit or register an application with the patent office, and “The inventor”. That is why it is “filed a patent”. It is countable and ends in t, without an e.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To register a patent: “file a patent”.
ejercicios.traduccion: El inventor registró una patente para su nuevo motor.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the Spanish word; in English it is spelt “patent”, without a final e.
A licence lets others use something; what protects an invention and is registered is a “patent”.

glosario.significado: registrar una patente, presentar la solicitud

descripcion_larga_es: Vocabulary for talking about research, innovation, the internet and artificial intelligence: research, findings, breakthrough, R&D, device, data breach, digital divide… It is essential for understanding the news and for discussing technology regulation or productivity. Many words look international, but the collocations change (carry out research, not make research), and there are uncountable nouns and false friends (research, evidence, actualize) that give Spanish speakers away.

contexto.que_es: It is the vocabulary of science (research, experiment, findings, evidence, peer review), innovation (R&D, patent, breakthrough) and digital technology (AI, algorithm, device, data breach, digital divide). What matters is not just the word, but which verb it combines with and whether it is countable or uncountable.
contexto.por_que_importa: These topics are everywhere in the press and in debates on the economy, productivity and regulation. Mistakes such as “a research”, “many evidences” or “make research” are very common among Spanish speakers and are noticed immediately. Using the right collocations (carry out research, file a patent) gives precision and naturalness.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When commenting on science or technology news, or talking about innovation policy, digitalisation or privacy. The signals are verbs such as publish, conduct, launch, download or file. Spanish speakers tend to calque “hacer una investigación” (make a research) or “actualizar” (actualize), and to make plural nouns that are uncountable in English.
